summary: NASA satellites capture vital signs of floods, heatwaves, droughts, and wildfires daily – yet the raw orbital data remains locked behind technical barriers for the people most affected. TerraTrace, created for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge, allows anyone to transform into a local climate investigator with one click. Drop a pin anywhere on Earth to compare 2015 and 2026 NASA GIBS imagery (MODIS True Color, Land Surface Temperature, and VIIRS Active Fires) and verify 21 years of NASA POWER climate shifts through 2040 with rigorous statistical testing (p < 0.05). This will produce zero-hallucination Google Gemini AI action plans tailored to that exact coordinate, bridging space science and frontline resilience for Awareness Today, Safety Tomorrow.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

TerraTrace turns complex NASA satellite data into simple local climate action. Users drop a pin anywhere on a map to compare 2015 versus 2026 NASA GIBS satellite views (heat maps, true color, and active fires). At the same time, it checks 21 years of NASA POWER temperature and rainfall data to confirm real climate trends through 2040 (p<0.05p < 0.05p<0.05) and uses Google Gemini AI to give clear safety and adaptation advice for that exact spot.

What benefits does it have and what is its intended impact?

It makes NASA science easy for anyone to understand without technical training, while proving whether local weather shifts are long-term trends or just short-term spikes. Our goal is to help farmers, local planners, and disaster teams protect crops, water, and lives early—delivering Awareness Today, Safety Tomorrow.

What tools, languages, hardware, and software did you use?

We built TerraTrace on standard laptops using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Python, hosted online via GitHub Pages / Netlify so it works on any phone or computer without installing software. It connects NASA GIBS and NASA POWER APIs with Leaflet.js (maps), Chart.js (graphs), a statistical trend calculator, and the Google Gemini API.

How is your project creative and what factors did your team consider?

Instead of giving generic climate tips, our AI bases every answer strictly on the real NASA numbers and 2040 forecast for the user's chosen pin, paired with a simple 2015-vs-2026 map switch. We focused on keeping the design simple, scientifically accurate, and fast-loading on slow mobile internet so rural farmers and local responders can use it anywhere.
